brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.evidence: A three-storey hex column (piece 0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2) with 9 hex-acc-hook plates.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: hex-acc-keyhole on face 3 of levels 0 and 2 (accessory:0#0,0#3, accessory:2#0,0#3), flat against the wall and lined up; meshes check clear. Holding strength depends on the wall screws and print material, which the configurator does not check.

hex-acc-hook plates on faces 0, 1 and 5 of every level, 18 hooks. Shown with gaffer tape and a cable coil only: the configurator refused to hang pliers, since only cable coils, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on hooks. Whether a given hand tool fits, and how much load a hook takes, is not checked.

finish.summary: Wall tool rack: three hex cells stacked in one column. Two keyhole hangers (levels 0 and 2) sit on face 3, flat against the wall and lined up. The opposite three faces (0, 1, 5) carry 9 hook plates, 18 hooks in all. Open faces are capped; the joint-locking step reported nothing to change. Staged with a gaffer tape roll and a cable coil on hooks, the only props the hooks accept; the coil can't be seen from straight in front. check_build: no rule errors, mesh check clear. 29 parts.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
